name: Thirteen Treasures of Britain

attributes.attribute: thirteen Otherworldly objects that show the rightful king
brought the treasures back from Annwn

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Thirteen Treasures of Britain is a British folkloric motif. Ireland had four great treasures brought from the Otherworld. They signified the sovereignty of the land. British lore names thirteen objects of Otherworldly origin. Those objects reside in this world. They betoken the rightful ruler. Arthur the great king carried them back from Annwn. Annwn is the Otherworld kingdom. The treasures include the sword of Rhydderch and a bottomless hamper. A mead-dispensing horn of Bran the Blessed serves the company. A speedy chariot and a halter that draws horses are part of the set. A knife replenishes the food it carves. A cauldron refuses to boil food for cowards. A whetstone sharpens only the weapons of the brave. A coat fits only the noblest warriors. A crock and a dish serve whatever the hungry desire.

okr.objective: Record the Thirteen Treasures of Britain as a sovereignty motif.
key_results: States that the treasures show the rightful king of Britain
Notes the role of King Arthur and the Otherworld kingdom Annwn
